name: zlib-ng
workload: CRC-32 checksumming of package/archive data (e.g. during Python pip install / wheel extraction), comparing zlib-ng's hardware-accelerated crc32 (SSE4.2/PCLMULQDQ/ARMv8 crypto) against stock zlib's table-based crc32, plus separate deflate compression/decompression benchmarks
claimed_speedup: "CRC: 10 to 100 times faster, using hardware CRC instructions", with observed throughput "as much as 600 GB/s on a desktop (AMD 7950X) for small data that can fit in CPU cache" vs zlib's non-accelerated crc32; separately, Red Hat's RHEL 10 docs report zlib-ng 2.2.3 overall decompression 378% faster and compression 423% faster than zlib (not CRC-specific)
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X desktop (crc32 numbers); RHEL 10 benchmarks used separate, unspecified hardware for the compression/decompression percentages
stars_or_usage: 2.1k stars; default zlib replacement in RHEL 10; used via LD_PRELOAD or direct linking in many Linux distros
tradeoffs: Ships a zlib-compat mode (ZLIB_COMPAT) for drop-in linking or LD_PRELOAD; CRC speedup depends on CPU support for PCLMULQDQ/SSE4.2/ARMv8 crypto extensions (falls back to a scalar/Chorba-optimized path otherwise); manual system-wide install is explicitly discouraged by the maintainers due to compatibility risk
caveats: The 10-100x / 600 GB/s CRC numbers come from a first-party-style engineering blog (Man Group, 8 May 2026) with CPU stated but no compiler/flags and a 'best of three runs on a laptop in battery-saving mode' methodology, not a formal reproducible benchmark suite -> capped at Tier C. The separately cited Red Hat RHEL 10 figures (378%/423%) are for overall compression/decompression, not isolated CRC32 performance.
found_via: vcpkg port 'zlib-ng' (ports/zlib-ng, REPO zlib-ng/zlib-ng) and conan-center-index recipe 'recipes/zlib-ng'; CRC benchmark evidence surfaced via the zlib-ng wiki 'In-the-media' page linking to https://www.man.com/technology/faster-python

name: libdeflate
workload: CRC-32 checksum computation via the public libdeflate_crc32() API; the repo ships a 'checksum' test program that can checksum data with Adler-32 or CRC-32 using either libdeflate or zlib and optionally measure speed
claimed_speedup: README states libdeflate "is significantly faster than the zlib library" (general claim covering compression/decompression/checksumming); no numeric CRC32-specific speedup is published in the current README
stars_or_usage: 1.3k stars; used as an optional/default backend in libtiff, htslib, OpenEXR, and uWebSockets
tradeoffs: Primarily a whole-buffer DEFLATE/zlib/gzip compressor; libdeflate_crc32() is a secondary utility function rather than the library's focus; no incremental/streaming-only CRC API beyond the single function call
caveats: No numeric CRC32 benchmark table is published in the current README (older revisions had compression benchmark tables that have since been removed); the 'significantly faster than zlib' claim is general and not isolated to crc32, so this is recorded at Tier D on notability grounds (1.3k stars, used in several widely-deployed C/C++ libraries) rather than on measured evidence.
found_via: vcpkg port 'libdeflate' and conan-center-index recipe 'recipes/libdeflate' (both point to REPO ebiggers/libdeflate)
